name: IL-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Biss's large fundraising advantage over an underfunded Republican
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
Open seat removes incumbency but not the partisan baseline
model.rationale: The seat's D+19 partisan lean, Biss's roughly $2.9 million in fundraising against a Republican with no reported finances, and markets pricing a Democratic win near 95% all point the same direction. The open seat adds modest uncertainty but nothing suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any sign of Republican outside spending or a contested primary fallout for Biss could narrow the margin, though a GOP win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jan Schakowsky (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Jan Schakowsky's retirement leaves this Chicago-area district open, but its strong Democratic lean keeps the seat firmly in the party's column. Daniel Biss enters the general election with a major financial edge, having raised nearly $3 million plus outside support, while Republican John Elleson shows no reported fundraising or outside spending.

Prediction markets give the Democratic nominee about a 95% chance of holding the seat, consistent with the district's D+19 partisan baseline. The open-seat transition introduces some uncertainty, but no polling or expert ratings suggest a competitive contest.
